entries.clue: Irishman joins church for spiritual event (6)

blocks.note: Sean is a typically Irish first name
CE = Church of England

annotation.surface: An Irishman goes along to church for some sort of religious gathering.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spiritual' reads as religious, which suits church; the event is actually a sitting to contact the dead.
annotation.definitionFit: A seance is a meeting at which people try to contact spirits.

entries.clue: Reported volume on speaking equipment is very shaky! (7)

indicatorNotes.Reported: what is reported is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: size = volume; SEIS is said the same way
a mic (microphone) is equipment for speaking into

annotation.surface: Someone complains that the sound level on the PA system is wobbling badly.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above. 'Volume' next to a microphone suggests loudness, but here it means bulk or capacity.
annotation.definitionFit: Seismic means of earthquakes, so shaking violently.

entries.clue: Play ground accommodates quiet exercise (5)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground as in crushed, so the letters of PLAY are broken up
indicatorNotes.accommodates: the rearranged word makes room for another letter inside it

blocks.note: PLAY rearranged
p = piano, quiet in music; it goes in after the A

annotation.surface: A playground has room for some quiet exercise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play ground' reads as the single word playground; split, it is fodder plus anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of putting something to use: you exercise or apply your judgement, your rights, pressure.

entries.clue: Kind to embrace darling getting reprimand (9)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: one word holds another in its arms

blocks.note: caring = kind
pet = darling, a favourite; it goes inside CAR…ING

annotation.surface: A gentle person hugs their sweetheart even while being told off.
annotation.walkthrough: Being 'carpeted' is British for being called in and scolded, from being summoned onto the boss's carpet.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: an employee called onto the boss's carpet is there to be scolded, so the noun means a reprimand.

entries.clue: One charging conservative customer on account (7)

blocks.note: ac is the usual abbreviation for account; 'on' puts what follows after it
C = Conservative
a user of a service is a customer

annotation.surface: A shop charges a Tory shopper's purchases to their account.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charging' looks like billing, which fits customer and account; it means bringing a charge against someone.
annotation.definitionFit: An accuser is one who charges someone with wrongdoing.

entries.clue: She has part in current version of Hair (7)

blocks.note: AC = alternating current
a tress is a lock of hair, another word for it

annotation.surface: A woman has a role in a new production of the musical Hair.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Hair look like the musical, which fits a part and a version; it is just hair.
annotation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman who has a part in a play.

entries.clue: Break off to deliver source of veal (5)

blocks.note: the glaciology sense: a chunk of ice breaking away from a glacier or ice shelf
veal comes from a calf, and 'deliver' is giving birth, as a cow does

annotation.surface: Someone stops work in order to hand over a supply of veal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deliver' sounds like a courier's job; here it is giving birth.
annotation.definitionFit: Calve means both to give birth to a calf and, of ice, to split away.

entries.clue: Attacks credit as a silly activity (9)

blocks.note: slaps = attacks with the hand
'on tick' is British slang for on credit

annotation.surface: Someone dismisses hitting out at credit as foolishness.
annotation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' means buying on credit, an old British phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous knockabout comedy, silly carry-on.

entries.clue: Alternative theatre, first time out, to produce warmed up fare (6)

blocks.note: the fodder word
t = time; the first T goes

annotation.surface: A fringe theatre company, opening for the first time, serves up reheated food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Alternative theatre' reads as fringe drama; 'Alternative' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: To reheat is to warm up food again.

entries.clue: Prohibit short-term teasing (6)

indicatorNotes.short: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: ban = prohibit
TERM with its last letter dropped

annotation.surface: A call to outlaw brief episodes of mockery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short-term' looks like one adjective, meaning temporary; split, it is an instruction to shorten TERM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: good-humoured ribbing between friends goes by either name.

entries.clue: Ship in colony worker – it’s vital (9)

blocks.note: to import is to ship goods in
a worker ant lives in a colony

annotation.surface: A worker is urgently sent by ship out to a colony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Colony' suggests empire, which fits shipping; it is an ant colony.
annotation.definitionFit: Important and vital both mean essential.

entries.clue: It secures request for silence on field (5)

blocks.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow; 'on' puts SH after it
sh! asks for quiet

annotation.surface: Someone manages to get quiet on the playing field.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Secures' reads as obtains, fitting the request; it means holds fast, as a lead holds a dog.
annotation.definitionFit: A leash is a lead that keeps an animal secure.

entries.clue: Vote in favour, blocking honour perhaps (5)

indicatorNotes.blocking: the vote sits in the middle, blocking the honour

blocks.note: MBE = Member of the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
ay (aye) is a yes vote; it goes inside M…BE

annotation.surface: A yes vote stands in the way of someone's honour.
annotation.walkthrough: The MBE is a British honour awarded in the King's lists.
annotation.definitionFit: Maybe and perhaps both express possibility.

entries.clue: Seated her awkwardly where there’s a lot of water (3,3,3)

annotation.definition: where there’s a lot of water

indicatorNotes.awkwardly: the letters are placed in an awkward, different order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Someone sat a woman clumsily in a damp spot.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: any sea would fit, which is why the anagram carries the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: The Red Sea is a large body of water between Africa and Arabia.

entries.clue: Copper is more reticent and less demanding (7)

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
shier = more shy

annotation.surface: A police officer is quieter and easier-going than colleagues.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer; it is the metal's symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: A cushy job is an easy one, so cushier means less demanding.

entries.clue: Evidence of accident near waste disposal area (9)

annotation.definition: Evidence of accident near waste disposal area

blocks.note: the surface reading: traces left on the road by a vehicle that braked and slid
the setter's joke: not beside a rubbish tip but close to the body's own exit, i.e. stains in underwear

annotation.surface: Investigators find traces of a crash beside the rubbish tip.
annotation.walkthrough: The waste disposal area is not a dump but the bottom; skidmarks is also British slang for stains in underpants.
annotation.definitionFit: Skid marks are the tyre streaks left when a vehicle skids.

entries.clue: King breaking cracked ice is taking a day off work! (6)

indicatorNotes.breaking: the K breaks into the other letters
indicatorNotes.cracked: the ice is cracked, so its letters are broken up

blocks.note: ICE IS rearranged
K = king in chess; it goes in after SIC

annotation.surface: A monarch fell through the ice and is now off work.
annotation.walkthrough: A sickie is British and Australian slang for a day off work claimed as sick leave, often falsely.
annotation.definitionFit: Taking a sickie is taking a day off, supposedly ill.

entries.clue: Being so numerous won’t matter so much (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the second definition splits the answer as the phrase COUNT LESS

blocks.note: too many to count
to count = to matter

annotation.surface: A large number of something makes each one less important.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a single idea; the break comes between 'numerous' and 'won't'.
annotation.definitionFit: Countless means too many to be counted.

entries.clue: Grumbled when husband leaving only hurt slightly (6)

indicatorNotes.leaving: a husband who is leaving walks out, so his letter H departs from WHINGED

blocks.note: whinged is British for complained
h = husband; it is removed from WHINGED

annotation.surface: Someone moaned when their husband left, though they were barely wounded.
annotation.walkthrough: To whinge is British English for to complain peevishly.
annotation.definitionFit: To wing someone is to shoot and wound them slightly, as a bird in the wing.

entries.clue: Composer badly used by son (7)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together badly, in a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
s = son, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A composer was mistreated by his own son.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Used by' reads naturally as part of the sentence, which hides it as fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Frenchman who wrote Clair de lune is one instance of the class.

entries.clue: Hoity-toity food with drink outside (5-2)

indicatorNotes.outside: the drink goes round the outside of the food

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
tuck is British schoolchild slang for food; it goes inside S…UP

annotation.surface: A snobbish meal served with drinks on the side.
annotation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for snacks, as in a tuck shop.
annotation.definitionFit: Stuck-up and hoity-toity both mean snobbishly superior.

entries.clue: Notice spotted showing what children can play with (3-3)

blocks.note: to see = to notice
saw = spotted, the past tense

annotation.surface: A sign has been seen listing what the playground offers children.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notice' looks like a noun, a sign; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a playground plank children ride up and down on.

entries.clue: Joke about woman, strictly religious (7)

indicatorNotes.about: the joke goes round, about, the woman

blocks.note: a pun is a joke on words
any woman's name can serve; RITA goes inside PU…N

annotation.surface: A gag about a woman who is very devout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woman' stands for a woman's first name; the crossings pin down which one.
annotation.definitionFit: Puritan describes someone strict in religion and morals.

entries.clue: Busier sketches becoming central for funny show (6)

indicatorNotes.central: take the central letters of each word

blocks.note: the middle two of BU-SI-ER
the middle two of SKE-TC-HES
the middle two of BEC-OM-ING

annotation.surface: Crowded sketches become the heart of a comedy programme.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' reads as a link word, but it is the third word to take letters from.
annotation.definitionFit: The genre name is short for situation comedy, so the definition describes the whole class of programme.

entries.clue: Setter can be silenced but will remain unchanged (9)

annotation.definitionNote: an adjective defined by what the thing does: something immutable will remain unchanged

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself: I'm = I am
able to be muted

annotation.surface: The setter may be shut up but won't change their ways.
annotation.walkthrough: MUTABLE is normally 'changeable'; here it is read literally as 'mute-able', which makes the surface's contrast a joke.
annotation.definitionFit: Defined by behaviour: the Latin roots mean 'not changeable', so whatever has this quality will stay as it is.

entries.clue: People find bone in empty temple (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the bone goes in the other letters
indicatorNotes.empty: the temple is emptied of its middle, leaving T…E

blocks.note: TEMPLE without its inside letters
a rib is a bone; it goes inside T…E

annotation.surface: Archaeologists dig up a bone in a deserted temple.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Empty' reads as deserted; it tells you to remove the middle of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A tribe is a people, a community of related families.

entries.clue: Root of initial trouble up by East Riding (5)

indicatorNotes.up: turned up, i.e. upside down, so read backwards

blocks.note: a but is an objection or snag, the first trouble raised
ER = East Riding, a former division of Yorkshire

annotation.surface: The origin of a problem that started up in the East Riding.
annotation.walkthrough: The East Riding was one of the three old divisions of the English county of Yorkshire.
annotation.definitionFit: A tuber, such as a potato, is a swollen underground root or stem.

entries.clue: Life with me is its own little world (5)

blocks.note: bio = life, as in biography
taken as written

annotation.surface: Someone declares that life with them is a world apart.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a partner's complaint; the definition is an ecological term.
annotation.definitionFit: A biome is a distinct natural community, such as tundra or rainforest.

entries.clue: Dog soldier joins military unit without further thought (5)

indicatorNotes.without: the unit loses the further thought

blocks.note: a corps is a military unit
a PS (postscript) is a further thought, removed from CORPS
GI = an American soldier

annotation.surface: A soldier impulsively signs up with an army unit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without further thought' reads as rashly; it instructs you to drop PS.
annotation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog.

entries.clue: Separated when tripping (6,3)

blocks.note: set at intervals, with gaps between
dazed, as on drugs

annotation.surface: People got split up when they stumbled.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tripping' looks like stumbling; it is drug slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Spaced out means both spread apart and dazed from drugs.

entries.clue: My container for flower shows great skill (7)

indicatorNotes.container for: MY is the container that the flower goes in

blocks.note: taken as written
the aster is a daisy-like flower; it goes inside M…Y

annotation.surface: Someone boasts that their flower vase displays real artistry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Container for flower' reads as a vase; it is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the skill of a master craftsman, as in a performance showing complete command.

entries.clue: Consignee’s sales hold back description of unwarranted items (2,4)

indicatorNotes.hold: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: consig-NEE'S SA-les

annotation.surface: A consignee's sales are being held up.
annotation.walkthrough: Goods 'sold as seen' come with no guarantee: the buyer accepts them in their present condition.
annotation.definitionFit: 'As seen' labels goods sold without warranty.
